title: Bar Graph Information Converted to a Table

illustrates.quote: Graphics with Identified Values. Tactile graphics are preferred, but a requester may ask that certain graphics be converted to a table. For example, a bar graph may show the value of each bar, lending itself to a table format. Explain the original format in a transcriber's note. Sample: The bar graph is presented as a table. (See Sample 11-20: Bar Graph Information Converted to a Table on page 11-44.)

print.caption: HEART ATTACKS IN THE UNITED STATES, 2000
print.notes: The print original is a horizontal bar graph (Age on the vertical axis, Attacks in thousands on the horizontal axis, separate blue/red bars for Males/Females with their values labeled directly on each bar), not a table; the braille converts it into an ordinary table.
print.printFeatures: Bar chart with a bold green two-line title, gridlines, an axis label ('Attacks in thousands'), a Males/Females color-coded legend, and a source line ('Source: American Heart Association') beneath the chart in italics.

braille.notes: Line 1 carries a transcriber's-note continuation marker token at the far right of the title line. A transcriber's note on lines 5-7 explains, in substance, that the print shows a horizontal bar graph and that in braille the graph has been changed to a table - matching the rule's own sample sentence. The source citation ('Source: American Heart Association') is transcribed on line 16, blocked in from the margin per rule 11.2.5.g.

resolution: print.rows: age ranges use an en dash ('29–44' etc.), matching print typography for numeric ranges (confirmed against the PDF image, p. 327) -- run B's plain hyphen was normalized to match run A. Same trailing-reference-code note as Sample 11-16 applies to line 1's length.
